Carpet traces

Source: R/zz-gen-carpet.R, R/zz-gen-figure.R
go_carpet.Rd

The data describing carpet axis layout is set in `y` and (optionally) also `x`. If only `y` is present, `x` the plot is interpreted as a cheater plot and is filled in using the `y` values. `x` and `y` may either be 2D arrays matching with each dimension matching that of `a` and `b`, or they may be 1D arrays with total length equal to that of `a` and `b`.

add_carpet(fig, ...)

# Default S3 method
add_carpet(
  fig,
  ...,
  data = NULL,
  a = NULL,
  a0 = NULL,
  aaxis = NULL,
  b = NULL,
  b0 = NULL,
  baxis = NULL,
  carpet = NULL,
  cheaterslope = NULL,
  color = NULL,
  customdata = NULL,
  da = NULL,
  db = NULL,
  font = NULL,
  ids = NULL,
  legend = NULL,
  legendgrouptitle = NULL,
  legendrank = NULL,
  legendwidth = NULL,
  meta = NULL,
  name = NULL,
  opacity = NULL,
  uid = NULL,
  uirevision = NULL,
  visible = NULL,
  x = NULL,
  xaxis = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  yaxis = NULL,
  zorder = NULL,
  row = NULL,
  col = NULL,
  secondary_y = NULL,
  skip_invalid = FALSE
)

Arguments

arg

Optional named list, or graph object of the same type, to initialise properties from (constructors). Named arguments take precedence.

...

Further properties, including nested properties in "magic underscore" form, e.g. marker_size = 10 for marker = list(size = 10). Property values may be one-sided formulas, evaluated in data for add_*() functions.

a

An array containing values of the first parameter value Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

a0

Alternate to `a`. Builds a linear space of a coordinates. Use with `da` where `a0` is the starting coordinate and `da` the step. Number.

aaxis

Named list or go_carpet_aaxis() object.

b

A two dimensional array of y coordinates at each carpet point. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

b0

Alternate to `b`. Builds a linear space of a coordinates. Use with `db` where `b0` is the starting coordinate and `db` the step. Number.

baxis

Named list or go_carpet_baxis() object.

carpet

An identifier for this carpet, so that `scattercarpet` and `contourcarpet` traces can specify a carpet plot on which they lie String.

cheaterslope

The shift applied to each successive row of data in creating a cheater plot. Only used if `x` is been omitted. Number.

color

go_carpet(), go_carpet_aaxis(), go_carpet_baxis(): Sets default for all colors associated with this axis all at once: line, font, tick, and grid colors. Grid color is lightened by blending this with the plot background Individual pieces can override this. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

go_carpet_aaxis_tickfont(), go_carpet_aaxis_title_font(), go_carpet_baxis_tickfont(), go_carpet_baxis_title_font(), go_carpet_font(), go_carpet_legendgrouptitle_font(): Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

customdata

Assigns extra data each datum. This may be useful when listening to hover, click and selection events. Note that, "scatter" traces also appends customdata items in the markers DOM elements Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

da

Sets the a coordinate step. See `a0` for more info. Number.

db

Sets the b coordinate step. See `b0` for more info. Number.

font

go_carpet(): The default font used for axis & tick labels on this carpet Named list or go_carpet_font() object.

go_carpet_aaxis_title(): Sets this axis' title font. Named list or go_carpet_aaxis_title_font() object.

go_carpet_baxis_title(): Sets this axis' title font. Named list or go_carpet_baxis_title_font() object.

go_carpet_legendgrouptitle(): Sets this legend group's title font. Named list or go_carpet_legendgrouptitle_font() object.

ids

Assigns id labels to each datum. These ids for object constancy of data points during animation. Should be an array of strings, not numbers or any other type. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

legend

Sets the reference to a legend to show this trace in. References to these legends are "legend", "legend2", "legend3", etc. Settings for these legends are set in the layout, under `layout.legend`, `layout.legend2`, etc. Subplot id: "legend", "legend2", "legend3", ....

legendgrouptitle

Named list or go_carpet_legendgrouptitle() object.

legendrank

Sets the legend rank for this trace. Items and groups with smaller ranks are presented on top/left side while with "reversed" `legend.traceorder` they are on bottom/right side. The default legendrank is 1000, so that you can use ranks less than 1000 to place certain items before all unranked items, and ranks greater than 1000 to go after all unranked items. When having unranked or equal rank items shapes would be displayed after traces i.e. according to their order in data and layout. Number.

legendwidth

Sets the width (in px or fraction) of the legend for this trace. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

meta

Assigns extra meta information associated with this trace that can be used in various text attributes. Attributes such as trace `name`, graph, axis and colorbar `title.text`, annotation `text` `rangeselector`, `updatemenues` and `sliders` `label` text all support `meta`. To access the trace `meta` values in an attribute in the same trace, simply use `%{meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` item in question. To access trace `meta` in layout attributes, use `%{data[n[.meta[i]}` where `i` is the index or key of the `meta` and `n` is the trace index. Any value.

name

go_carpet(): Sets the trace name. The trace name appears as the legend item and on hover. String.

go_carpet_aaxis_tickformatstop(), go_carpet_baxis_tickformatstop(): When used in a template, named items are created in the output figure in addition to any items the figure already has in this array. You can modify these items in the output figure by making your own item with `templateitemname` matching this `name` alongside your modifications (including `visible: false` or `enabled: false` to hide it). Has no effect outside of a template. String.

opacity

Sets the opacity of the trace. Number in the interval [0, 1].

uid

Assign an id to this trace, Use this to provide object constancy between traces during animations and transitions. String.

uirevision

Controls persistence of some user-driven changes to the trace: `constraintrange` in `parcoords` traces, as well as some `editable: true` modifications such as `name` and `colorbar.title`. Defaults to `layout.uirevision`. Note that other user-driven trace attribute changes are controlled by `layout` attributes: `trace.visible` is controlled by `layout.legend.uirevision`, `selectedpoints` is controlled by `layout.selectionrevision`, and `colorbar.(x|y)` (accessible with `config: {editable: true}`) is controlled by `layout.editrevision`. Trace changes are tracked by `uid`, which only falls back on trace index if no `uid` is provided. So if your app can add/remove traces before the end of the `data` array, such that the same trace has a different index, you can still preserve user-driven changes if you give each trace a `uid` that stays with it as it moves. Any value.

visible

Determines whether or not this trace is visible. If "legendonly", the trace is not drawn, but can appear as a legend item (provided that the legend itself is visible). One of "legendonly", TRUE, FALSE.

x

A two dimensional array of x coordinates at each carpet point. If omitted, the plot is a cheater plot and the xaxis is hidden by default. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

xaxis

Sets a reference between this trace's x coordinates and a 2D cartesian x axis. If "x" (the default value), the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis`. If "x2", the x coordinates refer to `layout.xaxis2`, and so on. Subplot id: "x", "x2", "x3", ....

y

A two dimensional array of y coordinates at each carpet point. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

yaxis

Sets a reference between this trace's y coordinates and a 2D cartesian y axis. If "y" (the default value), the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis`. If "y2", the y coordinates refer to `layout.yaxis2`, and so on. Subplot id: "y", "y2", "y3", ....

zorder

Sets the layer on which this trace is displayed, relative to other SVG traces on the same subplot. SVG traces with higher `zorder` appear in front of those with lower `zorder`. Integer.

skip_invalid

If TRUE, silently drop invalid properties instead of raising an error.

arraydtick

The stride between grid lines along the axis Integer in the interval [1, Inf].

arraytick0

The starting index of grid lines along the axis Integer in the interval [0, Inf].

autorange

Determines whether or not the range of this axis is computed in relation to the input data. See `rangemode` for more info. If `range` is provided, then `autorange` is set to FALSE. One of "reversed", TRUE, FALSE.

autotypenumbers

Using "strict" a numeric string in trace data is not converted to a number. Using "convert types" a numeric string in trace data may be treated as a number during automatic axis `type` detection. Defaults to layout.autotypenumbers. One of "convert types", "strict".

categoryarray

Sets the order in which categories on this axis appear. Only has an effect if `categoryorder` is set to "array". Used with `categoryorder`. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

categoryorder

Specifies the ordering logic for the case of categorical variables. By default, plotly uses "trace", which specifies the order that is present in the data supplied. Set `categoryorder` to "category ascending" or "category descending" if order should be determined by the alphanumerical order of the category names. Set `categoryorder` to "array" to derive the ordering from the attribute `categoryarray`. If a category is not found in the `categoryarray` array, the sorting behavior for that attribute will be identical to the "trace" mode. The unspecified categories will follow the categories in `categoryarray`. One of "trace", "category ascending", "category descending", "array".

cheatertype

One of "index", "value".

dtick

The stride between grid lines along the axis Number in the interval [0, Inf].

endline

Determines whether or not a line is drawn at along the final value of this axis. If TRUE, the end line is drawn on top of the grid lines. Logical.

endlinecolor

Sets the line color of the end line. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

endlinewidth

Sets the width (in px) of the end line. Number.

exponentformat

Determines a formatting rule for the tick exponents. For example, consider the number 1,000,000,000. If "none", it appears as 1,000,000,000. If "e", 1e+9. If "E", 1E+9. If "power", 1x10^9 (with 9 in a super script). If "SI", 1G. If "B", 1B. One of "none", "e", "E", "power", "SI", "B", "SI extended".

fixedrange

Determines whether or not this axis is zoom-able. If true, then zoom is disabled. Logical.

gridcolor

Sets the axis line color. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

griddash

Sets the dash style of lines. Set to a dash type string ("solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", or "longdashdot") or a dash length list in px (eg "5px,10px,2px,2px"). One of "solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", "longdashdot", or a string matching "^\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(px|%)?((,|\\s)\\s*\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(px|%)?)*$".

gridwidth

Sets the width (in px) of the axis line. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

labelalias

Replacement text for specific tick or hover labels. For example using {US: 'USA', CA: 'Canada'} changes US to USA and CA to Canada. The labels we would have shown must match the keys exactly, after adding any tickprefix or ticksuffix. For negative numbers the minus sign symbol used (U+2212) is wider than the regular ascii dash. That means you need to use -1 instead of -1. labelalias can be used with any axis type, and both keys (if needed) and values (if desired) can include html-like tags or MathJax. Any value.

labelpadding

Extra padding between label and the axis Integer.

labelprefix

Sets a axis label prefix. String.

labelsuffix

Sets a axis label suffix. String.

linecolor

Sets the axis line color. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

linewidth

Sets the width (in px) of the axis line. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

minexponent

Hide SI prefix for 10^n if |n| is below this number Number in the interval [0, Inf].

minorgridcolor

Sets the color of the grid lines. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

minorgridcount

Sets the number of minor grid ticks per major grid tick Integer in the interval [0, Inf].

minorgriddash

Sets the dash style of lines. Set to a dash type string ("solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", or "longdashdot") or a dash length list in px (eg "5px,10px,2px,2px"). One of "solid", "dot", "dash", "longdash", "dashdot", "longdashdot", or a string matching "^\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(px|%)?((,|\\s)\\s*\\d+(\\.\\d+)?(px|%)?)*$".

minorgridwidth

Sets the width (in px) of the grid lines. Number in the interval [0, Inf].

nticks

Specifies the maximum number of ticks for the particular axis. The actual number of ticks will be chosen automatically to be less than or equal to `nticks`. Has an effect only if `tickmode` is set to "auto". Integer in the interval [0, Inf].

range

Sets the range of this axis. If the axis `type` is "log", then you must take the log of your desired range (e.g. to set the range from 1 to 100, set the range from 0 to 2). If the axis `type` is "date", it should be date strings, like date data, though Date objects and unix milliseconds will be accepted and converted to strings. If the axis `type` is "category", it should be numbers, using the scale where each category is assigned a serial number from zero in the order it appears. Vector or list of 2 element(s).

rangemode

If "normal", the range is computed in relation to the extrema of the input data. If "tozero", the range extends to 0, regardless of the input data If "nonnegative", the range is non-negative, regardless of the input data. One of "normal", "tozero", "nonnegative".

separatethousands

If "true", even 4-digit integers are separated Logical.

showexponent

If "all", all exponents are shown besides their significands. If "first", only the exponent of the first tick is shown. If "last", only the exponent of the last tick is shown. If "none", no exponents appear. One of "all", "first", "last", "none".

showgrid

Determines whether or not grid lines are drawn. If TRUE, the grid lines are drawn at every tick mark. Logical.

showline

Determines whether or not a line bounding this axis is drawn. Logical.

showticklabels

Determines whether axis labels are drawn on the low side, the high side, both, or neither side of the axis. One of "start", "end", "both", "none".

showtickprefix

If "all", all tick labels are displayed with a prefix. If "first", only the first tick is displayed with a prefix. If "last", only the last tick is displayed with a suffix. If "none", tick prefixes are hidden. One of "all", "first", "last", "none".

showticksuffix

Same as `showtickprefix` but for tick suffixes. One of "all", "first", "last", "none".

smoothing

Number in the interval [0, 1.3].

startline

Determines whether or not a line is drawn at along the starting value of this axis. If TRUE, the start line is drawn on top of the grid lines. Logical.

startlinecolor

Sets the line color of the start line. Color: a CSS color string or R color name.

startlinewidth

Sets the width (in px) of the start line. Number.

tick0

The starting index of grid lines along the axis Number in the interval [0, Inf].

tickangle

Sets the angle of the tick labels with respect to the horizontal. For example, a `tickangle` of -90 draws the tick labels vertically. Angle in degrees.

tickfont

go_carpet_aaxis(): Sets the tick font. Named list or go_carpet_aaxis_tickfont() object.

go_carpet_baxis(): Sets the tick font. Named list or go_carpet_baxis_tickfont() object.

tickformat

Sets the tick label formatting rule using d3 formatting mini-languages which are very similar to those in Python. For numbers, see: https://github.com/d3/d3-format/tree/v1.4.5#d3-format. And for dates see: https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format/tree/v2.2.3#locale_format. We add two items to d3's date formatter: "%h" for half of the year as a decimal number as well as "%{n}f" for fractional seconds with n digits. For example, "2016-10-13 09:15:23.456" with tickformat "%H~%M~%S.%2f" would display "09~15~23.46" String.

tickformatstops

go_carpet_aaxis(): List of named lists or go_carpet_aaxis_tickformatstop() objects.

go_carpet_baxis(): List of named lists or go_carpet_baxis_tickformatstop() objects.

tickmode

One of "linear", "array".

tickprefix

Sets a tick label prefix. String.

ticksuffix

Sets a tick label suffix. String.

ticktext

Sets the text displayed at the ticks position via `tickvals`. Only has an effect if `tickmode` is set to "array". Used with `tickvals`. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

tickvals

Sets the values at which ticks on this axis appear. Only has an effect if `tickmode` is set to "array". Used with `ticktext`. Data array: a vector, factor, Date/POSIXct vector, matrix or list.

title

go_carpet_aaxis(): String (the title text), named list or go_carpet_aaxis_title() object.

go_carpet_baxis(): String (the title text), named list or go_carpet_baxis_title() object.

type

Sets the axis type. By default, plotly attempts to determined the axis type by looking into the data of the traces that referenced the axis in question. One of "-", "linear", "date", "category".

family

HTML font family - the typeface that will be applied by the web browser. The web browser can only apply a font if it is available on the system where it runs. Provide multiple font families, separated by commas, to indicate the order in which to apply fonts if they aren't available. String.

lineposition

Sets the kind of decoration line(s) with text, such as an "under", "over" or "through" as well as combinations e.g. "under+over", etc. Any combination of "under", "over", "through" joined with "+", or one of "none".

shadow

Sets the shape and color of the shadow behind text. "auto" places minimal shadow and applies contrast text font color. See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/text-shadow for additional options. String.

size

Number in the interval [1, Inf].

style

Sets whether a font should be styled with a normal or italic face from its family. One of "normal", "italic".

textcase

Sets capitalization of text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. One of "normal", "word caps", "upper", "lower".

variant

Sets the variant of the font. One of "normal", "small-caps", "all-small-caps", "all-petite-caps", "petite-caps", "unicase".

weight

Sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. Integer in the interval [1, 1000].

dtickrange

range ["min", "max"], where "min", "max" - dtick values which describe some zoom level, it is possible to omit "min" or "max" value by passing "null" Vector or list of 2 element(s).

enabled

Determines whether or not this stop is used. If `false`, this stop is ignored even within its `dtickrange`. Logical.

templateitemname

Used to refer to a named item in this array in the template. Named items from the template will be created even without a matching item in the input figure, but you can modify one by making an item with `templateitemname` matching its `name`, alongside your modifications (including `visible: false` or `enabled: false` to hide it). If there is no template or no matching item, this item will be hidden unless you explicitly show it with `visible: true`. String.

value

string - dtickformat for described zoom level, the same as "tickformat" String.

offset

An additional amount by which to offset the title from the tick labels, given in pixels. Number.

text

go_carpet_aaxis_title(), go_carpet_baxis_title(): Sets the title of this axis. String.

go_carpet_legendgrouptitle(): Sets the title of the legend group. String.

fig

A go_figure object.

data

A data frame in which formula properties (e.g. x = ~col, marker_size = ~col) are evaluated. Default: the data given to go_figure(). Only the evaluated values are added to the trace. A crosstalk::SharedData works the same way, and links the trace to its crosstalk group (see highlight()).

row

Subplot grid row (figures created with make_subplots() only). May be "all" or a vector to address several cells.

col

Subplot grid column (figures created with make_subplots() only). May be "all" or a vector to address several cells.

secondary_y

If TRUE, use the secondary y axis of the subplot.

Value

Each go_*() function returns a graph object of the same class as its name; add_*() functions return the modified figure.

Details

go_carpet() and the nested object constructors below create validated graph objects (named lists). Every property is checked against the plotly.js schema when an object is created or modified (see plotly_obj-modify()). add_carpet() creates an object and adds it to a figure.

Nested objects documented here:

go_carpet_aaxis()

carpet.aaxis

go_carpet_aaxis_tickfont()

carpet.aaxis.tickfont: Sets the tick font.

go_carpet_aaxis_tickformatstop()

carpet.aaxis.tickformatstop

go_carpet_aaxis_title()

carpet.aaxis.title

go_carpet_aaxis_title_font()

carpet.aaxis.title.font: Sets this axis' title font.

go_carpet_baxis()

carpet.baxis

go_carpet_baxis_tickfont()

carpet.baxis.tickfont: Sets the tick font.

go_carpet_baxis_tickformatstop()

carpet.baxis.tickformatstop

go_carpet_baxis_title()

carpet.baxis.title

go_carpet_baxis_title_font()

carpet.baxis.title.font: Sets this axis' title font.

go_carpet_font()

carpet.font: The default font used for axis & tick labels on this carpet

go_carpet_legendgrouptitle()

carpet.legendgrouptitle

go_carpet_legendgrouptitle_font()

carpet.legendgrouptitle.font: Sets this legend group's title font.

See also

go_figure(), add_trace()

Examples

go_carpet(x = 1:3, y = c(2, 1, 3))
#> <go_carpet>
#> {
#>   "type": "carpet",
#>   "x": [
#>     1,
#>     2,
#>     3
#>   ],
#>   "y": [
#>     2,
#>     1,
#>     3
#>   ]
#> }
#>
